cards.text: Paul, the apostle, has been held in prison for two years under Felix, the governor (Acts 24:27). Now Porcius Festus takes over from Felix, and three days after arriving in the province, Festus goes up from Caesarea to Jerusalem. THREE DAYS in and he's already on the road, friend, while three days into my bakery I was still opening every cupboard hunting for the cookie sheets.

cards.question: Festus has just arrived in Jerusalem. Who presents a case against Paul to him there?

answers.text: The chief priests and Jewish leaders

cards.text: The leaders urge Festus to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem. The governor is brand new, friend, and EVERYBODY wants something from the new guy.

cards.question: Why do the leaders want Festus to summon Paul from Caesarea to Jerusalem?

answers.text: To ambush and kill him on the way
To have him speak at the temple
To let the high priest question him

cards.text: But Festus replies, “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.”

cards.question: Festus won't summon Paul to Jerusalem. What does Festus tell the leaders to do if Paul has done anything wrong?

answers.text: Come down with him and accuse Paul there
Send their charges to him in a letter
Wait until Caesar can hear the case

cards.text: Festus spends no more than eight or ten days with them in Jerusalem. Then he heads back down to Caesarea.

cards.question: Festus is back in Caesarea. The next day, he sits on the judgment seat and orders that ___ be brought in.

cards.text: Paul is brought in, and the Jews who came down from Jerusalem stand all around him, bringing many serious charges they can't prove. Friend, if that many people circled me and pointed, I'd confess to eating cookies I never even touched.

cards.question: Surrounded by his accusers, Paul makes his defense. What does Paul tell Festus?

answers.text: He broke a minor temple rule

cards.question: Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, asks Paul if he's willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial.
Festus asks Paul to go up to Jerusalem for trial. Where does Paul say he ought to be tried?

answers.text: Before the judgment seat of Caesar

cards.text: Paul tells Festus he has done nothing wrong to the Jews, as Festus himself knows very well. That's looking the judge right in the eye, friend, and saying, YOU already know this.

cards.question: Paul says that if he's guilty of anything worthy of death, he does not refuse to die.

cards.text: But if there's no truth to their accusations, Paul says no one has the right to hand him over to them, and then he says, “I appeal to Caesar!” Friend, I can't even own up to one burnt batch without blaming the oven, and this man just put his LIFE on the table.

cards.question: Festus confers with his council, then turns down Paul's appeal to Caesar.

cards.text: Festus tells Paul, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!” Keep your apron on, friend, because Paul's road isn't done yet, and neither are we.
